acl.action: Prefer a vendor-coherent acl2.4 update with its new *_at ABI and rebuilt/migrated privileged callers; test tar compatibility. Do not transplant a single library patch or infer closure from deleting ACL CLIs.
acl.gate: Record native callers of acl_*_file and attacker-writable path ancestors, updated ABI consumers and symlink-race regression. Interim NNP/cap-drop and unprivileged, nonshared writable paths only reduce privilege impact.

apt.action: Retain explicit Signed-By and signed HTTPS repositories; never introduce apt-key/import of untrusted keyservers. Remove package-manager tooling from a separately validated final runtime only if no bootstrap/runtime requirement remains.
apt.gate: Compare the affected apt-key implementation with package file inventory, not apt package-name alone. Revalidate the current image after any slimming.

attr.action: Use vendor attr2.6 and fixed utilities where needed, otherwise omit the utilities from final runtime without removing required libattr transitively.
attr.gate: Prove affected getfattr/setfattr implementation absent or fixed and disallow privileged traversal of user-controlled ancestors.

bash.action: Retain vendor tracking; avoid identities crossing through shell environments. Run the service with NNP, dropped capabilities and no privileged diagnostic shell.
bash.gate: Review the referenced Debian bug and actual shell credential/environment transition. UID999 or no SSH is not a proof of absence.

bzip2.action: Update the bzip2recover utility from vendor/upstream fixed source if shipped; otherwise attest omission of this utility while retaining libbz2 needed by Python.
bzip2.gate: The CLI defect is not automatically a libbz2 decompression defect. Bind its absence to the actual current rootfs/package file list.

coreutils.action: Backport the specified utility fixes through vendor package builds. Avoid recursive privileged ownership operations on shared writable trees and untrusted utility option strings; final-runtime CLI slimming needs its own dependency and entrypoint validation.
coreutils.gate: Audit exact chown/chgrp, sort, uniq and unexpand calls, including maintenance/restore. Do not remove coreutils wholesale or treat lack of a Python textual hit as a complete call graph.

dash.action: Use fixed vendor shell builds when available. Keep entrypoint arguments constant and never form dash -c/printf/echo format or glob expressions from external data.
dash.gate: Determine libc-fnmatch build option and actual builtin paths. Shell exists; bounds and restricted inputs reduce exposure without repairing it.

diffutils.action: Apply upstream diff3 arithmetic fixes through a reproducible vendor package, or omit diff3 from a validated final runtime. Do not allow attacker-selected --diff-program.
diffutils.gate: Inventory diff3 and maintenance workflows; supplying a different working directory does not repair arithmetic.

gcc-14.action: Review GCC14 vendor fixes and separate exported libstdc++ code from header/template-instantiated code. Update runtime libraries for out-of-line code; rebuild affected native consumers against fixed headers where required.
gcc-14.gate: Inventory DT_NEEDED plus statically linked/template code in the actual native wheels. Missing gcc executable/headers and a newer libstdc++ alone cannot prove closure.

glibc.action: Prefer supported Debian trixie security/point backports or a separately validated coherent base. Do not apt-mix sid libc into the candidate. Bound untrusted native inputs and remove privilege paths as mitigations, keeping IDs open until affected implementation or exact precondition is resolved.
glibc.gate: Resolve each API/architecture/precondition below; patch/rebuild tests must cover runtime DNS, locale/conversion and SUID loader behavior, not only Python package audit.

ncurses.action: Backport infocmp/termcap fixes through Debian-compatible package builds. If infocmp is unnecessary, remove that utility in a separate tested final-stage change while preserving readline/libtinfo dependencies.
ncurses.gate: infocmp exists in the captured rootfs, so the HIGH cannot be dismissed because no TTY or interactive UI is expected. Review imported terminfo/termcap and native callers.

pam.action: Inventory installed PAM configuration/modules and exclude pam_userdb plaintext authentication from container and operational paths; use vendor timing fix when available.
pam.gate: FastAPI bcrypt is separate from PAM and does not prove PAM unreachable. Account/maintenance services and mounted host configurations must be addressed.

perl.action: Use vendor fixes for Perl regex/File::Temp, Archive::Tar3.10 and Pod::Text6.1.1 as appropriate. Avoid processing untrusted data through system Perl in runtime/restore, and omit unnecessary modules in a separately validated image.
perl.gate: Archive::Tar and Pod::Text are modules, distinct from GNU tar or systemd logging. Verify @INC/module payload in current image; perl-base and regex/File::Temp remain present.

shadow.action: Remove unnecessary SUID/SGID account-management entry points or enforce NNP as a separately verified deployment control. Lock authentication logs and subordinate-ID policy to trusted configuration; follow vendor fixes.
shadow.gate: Inventory chfn/chsh/su and modes, btmp permissions, subuid/subgid and shared/NFS mounts. Lack of sshd or newuidmap alone does not resolve the whole source group.

sqlite3.action: Use a vendor-fixed SQLite build including applicable Session changes. Disable extension loading and do not consume untrusted database/changeset/ZIP files in runtime/restore; keep bounded SQL/data inputs.
sqlite3.gate: Production primary-DB rejection of SQLite is not sufficient: catalog/legacy SQLite call sites exist. Separate zipfile extension, Session v2/v3/shared helpers and malformed database exposure.

systemd.action: Keep unneeded service payload omitted and do not mount host service sockets/config into the app. If adding those services later, apply the vendor fixes before enabling them.
systemd.gate: Installed libsystemd0/libudev1 does not establish presence of homed/oomd/journald/tmpfiles. Conversely process-not-running is weaker than source-component/payload absence; current-rootfs proof is still needed.

sysvinit.action: Do not ship/use an installer or emergency-login configuration permitting passwordless root recovery; remove unnecessary recovery utilities only after entrypoint/maintenance validation.
sysvinit.gate: Review the original installer/sulogin scenario and root-account configuration. A web CMD alone does not attest all recovery paths.

tar.action: Backport applicable GNU tar fixes via vendor builds and validate restore independently. Never rely on --one-top-level, fresh extraction directory or listing-before-extract as sole security boundary; avoid untrusted archives and privileged extraction.
tar.gate: Constrain archive entries, hardlinks/symlinks and file metadata, preserve no-privilege extraction and separate destination. Treat rmt as its own executable/protocol; GNU tar differs from Perl Archive::Tar.

util-linux.action: Prefer trixie-coherent builds with upstream stable2.41.6 fixes or later vendor backports; Debian unstable fixed versions are references, not permission to mix sid packages. Remove unneeded mount SUID and enforce NNP/cap-drop/no host namespaces as separately tested mitigations; prohibit privileged nsenter --join-cgroup into untrusted targets.
util-linux.gate: Retain mount/libmount/nsenter/login provenance and test the exact fixed paths. Empty fstab and kernel6.1 are lab observations, not deployment invariants or patches.

xz-utils.action: Keep exact liblzma5 u2 package/hash/version checks in both shared stages; no rollback to u1 or legacy backend fallback.
xz-utils.gate: Verified same-database scanner delta removes only these two aliases. This is not a fix for the other20 source groups.

zlib.action: Review/backport crc32 length validation and gzwrite fix separately in vendor zlib, checking introduced-code ranges. Avoid unbounded/negative CRC-combine lengths and affected nonblocking gz* sequences until fixed.
zlib.gate: Map actual system and vendored wheel copies; Python compress/decompress use does not imply crc32_combine or gzprintf use. An exported symbol list alone cannot show all static internal implementations.
